scope: Configuration-specific audit of the files selected by the pinned Android ARM64 build (subtarget=lucent, sources=src/mame/atari/pong.cpp,src/mame/snk/neogeo.cpp,src/mame/snk/neogeocd.cpp), determined by intersecting every licence-tagged source in the tree against the 1049 object files the build actually produced under build/. No game, firmware, or prebuilt dependency is included. This engineering record is not legal advice.
aggregateConclusion: Not blocked. Exactly three of the 1049 linked objects come from GPL-tagged sources, and all three are tagged GPL-2.0+ (or-later), which is compatible with Lucent's GPL-3.0-only combined distribution. No file anywhere in the tree carries a GPL-2.0-only tag. The aggregate licence is also or-later: docs/source/license.rst in this same pinned commit states 'The MAME project as a whole is distributed under the terms of the GNU General Public License, version 2 or later (GPL-2.0+), since it contains code made available under multiple GPL-compatible licenses.' and its copyright block grants 'either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.' Copyright compatibility is therefore established at both the file level and the aggregate level. The remaining risk is not copyright but trademark: see openQuestions.
method: Enumerated every '// license:' tag under src/. Distribution: 13998 BSD-3-Clause, 434 GPL-2.0+, 196 LGPL-2.1+, 113 CC0-1.0, 77 MIT, 6 BSD-2-Clause, 5 GPL2+, 2 Public, 1 bare GPL. Zero GPL-2.0-only tags.

Listed the 1049 object files under build/ and matched each candidate GPL/LGPL source to its object by full path, not basename. Basename matching alone produced 12 apparent hits, 9 of which were unrelated same-named files in unbuilt directories (for example src/devices/bus/vtech/memexp/memory.cpp versus the compiled 3rdparty/flac/src/libFLAC/memory.o).
Audited every 3rdparty component that produced objects, since the prior registry note flagged dependencies as unaudited.

components.evidence: All three target drivers carry '// license:BSD-3-Clause' in their header comments.
The emulation framework, OSD layer and netlist library that the drivers link against are BSD-3-Clause. src/lib/netlist tags are 182 BSD-3-Clause and 43 CC0-1.0, with no GPL tag.

The only GPL-licensed code linked into the core. Each carries '// license:GPL-2.0+' with copyright-holders 'DICE Team,Couriersud'. They are unavoidable in this scope: pong.cpp includes nl_breakout.h, nl_rebound.h and nl_pongdoubles.h directly at lines 61-64, because Breakout and Rebound are discrete-logic titles implemented in the same driver as Pong. The '+' makes these upgradeable to GPL-3.0 at the recipient's option, so they are compatible.
The only two LGPL objects linked, both tagged '// license:LGPL-2.1+'. The or-later grant permits LGPL-3.0, which is GPL-3.0 compatible.

309 objects, the largest third-party component. COPYING.txt identifies it as 'License for Berkeley SoftFloat Release 3e', a plain three-clause BSD grant. This is materially different from the legacy SoftFloat 2b terms that block beetle-vb: Release 3e carries no indemnification or responsibility clause. See beetle-vb-license.json for the contrasting case.

Only libFLAC objects are built (27). libFLAC source headers carry the Xiph.Org three-clause BSD grant. The COPYING.GPL and COPYING.FDL files in 3rdparty/flac cover the command-line tools and documentation respectively, neither of which is compiled here.
Dual-licensed. LICENSE is the Meta Platforms BSD grant and COPYING is GPL-2.0. Lucent elects the BSD option, which carries no copyleft obligation.

components.license: Permissive (MIT / BSD / zlib / IJG / public domain)
components.evidence: All remaining third-party components that produced objects are permissive. Lua and the Lua bindings are MIT, utf8proc and expat and zlib and ymfm carry their own permissive notices, lzma and sqlite3 are public domain, and libjpeg is the Independent JPEG Group licence acknowledged in MAME's own COPYING at line 26.

refutedClaims.claim: MAME is GPL-2.0-only, so the core cannot ship in a GPL-3.0-only distribution.
refutedClaims.finding: No file in the pinned tree carries a GPL-2.0-only tag. Every GPL tag present is an or-later grant (434 GPL-2.0+ and 5 GPL2+). The registry's existing spdx value of GPL-2.0-or-later matches the tag on the only GPL files that actually compile.

refutedClaims.claim: A driver cannot run without the GPL-2.0-only MAME framework, so the framework taints the build.
refutedClaims.finding: The framework is not GPL. src/emu, src/osd, src/devices and src/lib/netlist are BSD-3-Clause, as are all three target drivers. The GPL-2.0-or-later code reaching the link is three Pong-family netlist translation units, not the framework.

resolvedQuestions.question: COPYING lines 16-18 grant 'the GNU General Public License version 2, as provided in docs/legal/GPL-2.0' with no 'or later' clause, and docs/legal contains no GPL-3.0 text. Read alone that is a GPL-2.0-only grant over the collective work, which would be incompatible.
resolvedQuestions.resolution: Resolved in favour of or-later by two other statements in the same pinned commit. docs/source/license.rst lines 5-7: 'The MAME project as a whole is distributed under the terms of the GNU General Public License, version 2 or later (GPL-2.0+), since it contains code made available under multiple GPL-compatible licenses.' Its copyright block at lines 17-20 grants 'either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.' docs/source/whatis.rst line 52 repeats the GPL-2.0+ characterisation. These address the project as a whole explicitly and are more specific than COPYING's terse wording. COPYING lines 4-7 point the same way by delegating to per-file headers: 'Individual source files may be made available under less restrictive licenses, as noted in their respective header comments.' license.rst also corroborates this audit's file census independently, stating that over 90% of files including core files are 3-Clause BSD; the measured figure here is about 94%.

openQuestions: TRADEMARK, not copyright, and the only live risk. docs/source/license.rst lines 12-13: 'Please note that MAME is a registered trademark of Gregory Ember, and permission is required to use the “MAME” name, logo, or wordmark.' COPYING line 1 repeats the registration. Lucent currently uses the bare string 'MAME' as registry displayName and in the packaged artefact name liblucent_core_mame.so. Nothing in the GPL grant conveys trademark rights, so this needs either written permission from the mark holder or a rename to a non-infringing descriptive label before shipping.
followUps: Resolve the trademark question above before shipping: obtain permission, or rename the user-facing engine label and the packaged core artefact to something that does not use the MAME name, logo, or wordmark.
Re-run this audit if the pinned commit, the sources= list, or the subtarget changes, since the file-level conclusion is scope-specific and widening scope can pull in GPL-tagged drivers.
